doc: GET: Returns the "new circular" state for the current session.
My rule (B1 — 24h window for both states):
- A circular is a *candidate* only if uploaded within the window.
- Logged-in: a candidate is "unread" until the user opens it. Reading every candidate clears the dot early.
- Logged-out: every candidate is "unread" (no per-user read state); the dot rides out the window regardless of who viewed it.
Response: { hasNewCircular: boolean, unreadIds: number[] } unreadIds = the recent circulars this session should show as unread (used by the modal to bold their titles).

doc: Decides when the search window's code is fetched: "idle" = once the page is interactive and the browser has nothing better to do (new); "now" = at once when the page starts (closest to the previous way, where it came with the page).

doc: Decides when the guide's code is fetched: "pointer" = when the pointer reaches the Help button, or on its click (new); "now" = at once when the page starts.

switches.name: skipUnusedHomeLinks
doc: true: the three link lists that the new home page never draws are not read from the database (new). false: I read them on every visit (previous).

switches.name: localNewsThumbs
doc: true: I draw the three news thumbnails on the page itself (new). false: they are fetched from placehold.co, an outside site (previous).

switches.name: deferHomeVideo
doc: true: the plant video starts once the page has loaded, and the hero picture shows meanwhile (new). false: it starts loading with the page (previous).

switches.name: optimisedHeroPicture
doc: true: the hero picture is the lighter copy public/steel-plant1.opt.jpg, fetched early (new). false: the 697 KB original (previous).

switches.name: rightSizedLogos
doc: true: the two logos ask for a picture of the size they are drawn at, not 1024 px (new). false: sizes as declared before (previous).

switches.name: cssVideoHover
doc: true: the pause symbol over the video shows on hover by CSS alone, so the page is not drawn again at each mouse move over it (new). false: the hover is held in React state (previous).

switches.name: holidaysOnCalendarTab
doc: true: I fetch the holidays when the Calendar tab is first opened (new). false: they are fetched on every page load, though Birthdays is the tab that shows (previous).

switches.name: pauseOffscreenScrollers
doc: true: the three auto-scrolling lists stand still while they are off the screen (new). false: they scroll all the time (previous).

switches.name: feedFocusThrottleSeconds
doc: Seconds: the announcements list is asked for again when the window is focused again, at most once in this time (new: 60). Previous: 5 (the library's own value).

switches.name: parallelReads
doc: true: independent database reads of one request run together (new). false: they run one after the other (previous).

switches.name: parallelAnnouncementSearch
doc: true: the four queries of the announcement search run together (new). false: they run one after the other (previous).

switches.name: installPgExtensionsAtStart
doc: true: TypeORM asks the database to install the vector extension at every cold start (previous). false: it is not asked, because the extension is already installed (new).

switches.name: prefetchQueryEmbedding
doc: true: I request the question's embedding while the language model is still deciding where the question belongs, so it is ready when the circular search needs it (new). false: it is asked for only then (previous).

switches.name: slimCircularReads
doc: true: reading a circular for its title or its viewer takes only the columns that are used, not the 768-number embedding and the whole text (new). false: the whole row is read (previous).

switches.name: routerCacheSeconds
doc: Seconds a router decision (which tool a question belongs to) is remembered for the same question (new: 600). 0 = never remembered (previous).

switches.name: nl2sqlExamplesCacheSeconds
doc: Seconds the list of confirmed and rejected example queries is remembered (new: 90; a new vote shows up in the model's prompt within this time). 0 = read on every question (previous).

switches.name: peopleEventsCacheSeconds
doc: Seconds the CDN may keep the home page's People & Events lists (new: 120). 0 = never cached (previous).

switches.name: browserCacheFontsAndVideo
doc: true: fonts and the plant video are kept for a week in the browser (new). false: they are asked of the server on every visit (previous). Read by next.config.js.

switches.name: edsDrafts
doc: ---------------------------------------------------------------- Executive Deep Search (src/lib/search/executiveSynthesis.ts)

"hedged": ONE draft is written, and a second only when the first is late (see edsHedgeSeconds) (new). "both": two drafts side by side, the better one kept (previous: it waited for the slower of the two and paid for both).

switches.name: edsHedgeSeconds
doc: Seconds: a model call (a draft, the repair, the second reading) that has not answered after this long is sent a second time and the first answer to arrive is used, so a call that hangs costs this, not its 45 s timeout (new: 20). 0 = never (previous).

switches.name: edsVerifyDuringRepair
doc: true: the second reading of the best draft starts at once, side by side with the repair attempt, and the repaired answer is read again only if the repair is kept (new). false: the reading waits for the repair (previous).

switches.name: allowProModels
doc: false: a Pro model (gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-pro-latest ...) is REFUSED everywhere, whatever asks for it: a code default, an environment variable, a script (new: my order of 23 Nov 2026, src/lib/ai/noPro.ts). true: Pro models may be used (previous).

switches.name: edsDraftModel
doc: The model that WRITES a briefing: "gemini-3.8-flash" (new: 7 to 17 s a draft, against 11 to 17 s for pro on the same circulars, and as many key facts found in the gold test: scripts/eds-gold.ts). "" = gemini-3.1-pro-preview (previous). The environment (GEMINI_SYNTHESIS_MODEL) overrides it.

switches.name: edsVerifyModel
doc: The model that CHECKS a briefing against the circulars (the second reading): "gemini-3.8-flash" (new: 2 to 7 s, against 8 to 22 s for pro; it caught every error planted in four briefings, as pro did). "" = the writer's model (previous: pro). The environment (GEMINI_VERIFY_MODEL) overrides it.

header: 01_nlq_schema_views_role.sql EXPERIMENT: natural-language -> SQL written by the LLM. This file creates the ONLY objects the LLM-written SQL may touch, and the role it runs as. I keep it additive and idempotent: nothing existing is modified or dropped.

PREREQUISITES (already in your database, per earlier sessions): public.employee_roster, public.designation_grade, public.sail_department, public."user", and the phonetic functions public.indic_fold(text), public.name_synonym_normalize(text, boolean), public.name_phonetic_codes(text).
SECURITY MODEL
* The LLM's SQL runs as role nlq_reader, inside a READ ONLY transaction, with a statement timeout (see executor.ts).
* nlq_reader can SELECT only from the three views below and EXECUTE only nlq.norm / nlq.code. It has NO privilege on public."user" (passwords, tokens), employee_roster, or anything else.

* I deliberately expose NO phone numbers, email addresses or street addresses in the views -- only yes/no flags such as has_email_nic -- so a query can COUNT people without email but can never READ an address.
Run this whole file at once.

02_nl2sql_log_tables.sql This logs every question, the SQL the model wrote, the outcome and the person's tick/cross. I feed confirmed (ticked) question/SQL pairs back to the model as worked examples -- that is how the system improves WITHOUT code changes. Additive and idempotent. nlq_reader has no privilege on this table.
03_optional_dedicated_login_role.sql (RECOMMENDED for production use)

Why I want it: with only 01_*.sql the application runs the LLM's SQL by switching its own connection to nlq_reader (SET ROLE). The guard (guard.ts) blocks the one known way out of that (calling set_config('role', ...)), but a dedicated LOGIN role removes the possibility entirely: nlq_app is a member of nlq_reader and of nothing else, so it can never switch to a more powerful role no matter what SQL runs.
Steps:
1. Run this file (choose your own password below).
2. Set NL2SQL_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://nlq_app:<password>@<same host as DATABASE_URL>/<db> in the environment. The experiment then uses its own connection.

04_fix_name_codes_permission.sql This fixes "permission denied for schema public" when a query uses name_codes / the name-matching helpers. Run this whole file once on the live database. Safe to re-run. NOTE: SUPERSEDED. 05_fast_name_codes.sql and 06_spelling_families.sql replace this file. Do NOT run 04 after 05 or 06: it would put back an older version of nlq.name_codes_of (without the spelling rule). (I updated 01_nlq_schema_views_role.sql to include the same change for fresh installs.)

05_fast_name_codes.sql This makes phonetic name matching fast (a query that took 6.4 s now takes milliseconds). Run this whole file once on the live database. Safe to re-run, in any order with 06. It adds ONE new table and replaces the view and the three helper functions; it changes no existing table.

Why it was slow: the phonetic code of every name was recomputed for every employee, several times per query. Now I store the codes once, and the helpers are plain SQL the database can optimise (they were needlessly SECURITY DEFINER, which stops that).

Correctness is self-protecting: I use a stored row only if its stored NAME still equals the employee's current name; otherwise the code is computed live. So a renamed or brand-new employee is never answered from stale data. After changing the phonetic functions themselves (e.g. adding a synonym), run: SELECT nlq.refresh_name_codes();

06_spelling_families.sql This teaches the name search that spelling variants of the -padhyay surnames are the same name: Mukhopadhya / Mukhopadhayay -> Mukhopadhyay (= Mukherjee), Gangopadhya -> Gangopadhyay (= Ganguly = Ganguli), likewise Bandyopadhya (= Banerjee) and Chattopadhya (= Chatterjee). Also: Bhattacharya = Bhattacharyya = Bhattacharjee = Bhattacharji = Bhattacharjya (and the typo Bhattacharyay). Also (31, 22 Nov 2026): Datta and Datt are written Dutta (the Bengali surname is one name; the directory has both spellings). Only words that START with Bhattachar and END in a -ya / -yya / -jee / -ji / -jya form are touched; Bhatia, Bhattar etc. are not. Works for typed words and for stored names. I keep this inside the nlq schema: my phonetic functions in schema public are NOT changed, so the old omnibar search is unaffected. Run this whole file once. Safe to re-run. (A fresh install needs only 01, which now includes this.)

07_feedback_learning.sql This is the learning loop: I record a Yes/No on EVERY omnibar answer (model, cache, holiday, old engine, circular results), with the reason for a No, plus the columns that let a "No" trigger a different second attempt and let confirmed / rejected answers teach the model. Additive and idempotent: run this whole file once on the live database (a fresh install already gets the same objects from 02).
public.nl2sql_log gains: source ('nl2sql'|'cache'), retry_of (the answer this one replaced), reject_reason, reject_note public.omnibar_feedback NEW: one row per Yes/No click, for any kind of answer.

08_health_checkups.sql The monthly HEALTH CHECK-UP schedules of non-executive employees (an annexure of a circular), as data: who is called on which date. Filled by scripts/import-health-checkups.ts, which reads the roster pages (the date of a group is printed once in a merged cell: it is taken from that cell's ruled lines) and checks every row against the HR directory. Additive and idempotent. Run this whole file at once.

status: 'verified' ticket and name agree with the HR directory 'corrected' the ticket was misread; the one HR employee with this name and department was used (status_note says so) 'unverified' not confirmed against HR (usually a person no longer in the HR directory). The table keeps ticket_no NULL for these; the VIEW below still shows the ticket as PRINTED in the circular, with verified = false (Yes/No on screen), so I never show a person without their ticket. Two cases are NOT shown with a ticket, because it may belong to someone else: the printed ticket is another HR employee's (status_note "belongs to") or appears twice in the schedule.
09_circular_ingest_log.sql

I keep here what the upload DECIDED about each circular, one row per upload: which kind it recognised, what it did, and why. Nothing reads this to answer a question; it is the backend's memory, so that I can answer "why is there no health check-up data for this circular?" by looking:
SELECT c.id, c."serialNumber", l.kind, l.status, l.detail, l.created_at FROM public.circular_ingest_log l JOIN public.circulars c ON c.id = l.circular_id ORDER BY l.id DESC LIMIT 10;

kind: 'health-schedule' the pages hold a roster table (T.No / Name / Deptt.Code / Department / Date): read into health_checkup_schedule 'holiday-list' the employee holiday-list circular: display only (its facts are seeded from a curated file) 'general' anything else: read, chunked and embedded as always status: 'applied' a health schedule was read, checked against HR and stored 'needs-review' it was read but something looked wrong (the detail says what): NOT stored; run scripts/import-health-checkups.ts to look 'timeout' the upload ran out of time before it could finish reading the schedule: run the tool 'failed' the reading or the storing failed (the detail says why): run the tool 'saved' a general or holiday-list circular, saved as usual

Rows go with their circular (ON DELETE CASCADE), so a deleted and re-uploaded circular starts with a clean history. Safe to run more than once. I made the upload keep working if this table does not exist: it writes the log only when it can.

10_circular_page_check.sql Here I store what a SECOND READER (Gemini) said about the numbers of each page of a circular: which numbers both readings had ("confirmed") and which only the pipeline's reading had ("unconfirmed"). The answer card refuses a number that is unconfirmed (src/lib/search/circularAnswer.ts, the confirmation gate). "text_hash" is the fingerprint of the page's stored text at the time of the check: I use a check only while the stored text still has that hash, so a re-read circular's old check is ignored. Written only by: npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/crosscheck-report.ts --ids ... --apply
Run ONE SECTION AT A TIME in the Supabase SQL editor: it shows only the last statement's result when several run together.

11_doctor_flag.sql (step 48b) Doctors and non-medical executives. I count a person as a doctor if he is on the MEDICAL track of designation_grade, or is flagged here: a few doctors carry a normal managerial designation (an eye specialist who is a "Sr. Manager" in the HR tool) and I must not touch their designation. nlq.employees gets ONE more column, at the end: is_doctor. Idempotent. The live data change (which people to flag) is in cleanup/sql/48b_doctor_flag_live.sql, not here.

11_feedback_source_hospital.sql (step 61a) WHY: the Yes/No feedback of an answer is recorded against the route that produced it (omnibar_feedback.source). The column only allows 'nl2sql', 'cache', 'holiday', 'legacy', 'circular', 'none', so I tag the hospital route's answers 'holiday' (a known, harmless fudge). This step lets the column also hold 'hospital'. NOTHING in the app writes 'hospital' yet: I change the app only AFTER this step has run (otherwise a Yes/No on a hospital answer would be refused). HOW: run ONE SECTION AT A TIME in the Supabase SQL editor (it shows only the last statement's result when several run together). 1 CHECK (read-only) -> 2 FIX (one guarded transaction: it aborts on anything unexpected; if it errors, run ROLLBACK;) -> 3 VERIFY (read-only).

13_pax_admin.sql : the PAX admin panel (step 64a). Run ONCE in the Supabase SQL editor. It only ADDS two tables; public.pax_directory is not changed. pax_delegate the executives the HOD C&IT has authorised to change PAX numbers (I keep a revoked line, with who revoked it and when) pax_directory_audit one line for every add, change, delete, authorisation and revocation, with who did it (ticket and name from the login) and the line before and after. APPEND ONLY. Like pax_directory, both are closed to the public API roles: only the application's own connection reads and writes them.
14_people_events.sql : date of birth and date of joining for the "People & Events" widget (steps 65a, 65b). Run in the Supabase SQL editor; safe to run again (see the note on re-running).
WHAT IT DOES

1. adds three columns to public.employee_roster (the table of ALL employees): date_of_birth date (a calendar date: no time, no time zone, so no day can ever shift) date_of_joining date dates_source text 'hr' = a real date from the HR records, 'synthetic' = a PLACEHOLDER made up by this file
2. makes the database itself refuse a wrong pair of dates, so that no later import, by anybody, can break the rules:
* nobody joins before the age of 18;

* an executive who joined DIRECTLY (a Management Trainee: ticket 49xxxx) not before 23. (The ceiling of 32 at joining, the age limit of a recruitment advertisement, is kept in the placeholders below but I do NOT enforce it here: a real record may carry an age relaxation.)

3. makes up PLACEHOLDER dates for every employee that has no real date, because the HR department has not supplied them yet (this is a development database with sample data). They are made up from the ticket number, so running this file again gives the same dates; they are tied to seniority (a General Manager is not 26 years old); the age at joining is spread EVENLY between the minimum (18, or 23 for a direct-recruit executive) and 32, the ceiling of a recruitment advertisement, so not everybody joins at the minimum; and every one satisfies the rules above and is still "in service" today (nobody is past the retirement day, which is the last day of the month in which the age of 60 is reached). WHERE THE DATES LIVE (my decision, 1 Nov 2026): as columns of employee_roster, next to the person, not in a separate table. THE ONE RULE THAT GOES WITH IT: if the roster is ever reloaded from an HR export, UPDATE or UPSERT the rows by ticket number and NEVER empty, drop or re-create the table, because the three date columns (and the sample dates in them) would go with it. I created NO INDEX on purpose: the widget reads the roster (about 6,500 rows) once per page view, and the test measured that read at a few milliseconds. An index on these date expressions would only add work to every write. Add expression indexes if the roster ever grows past about 100,000 rows. A REAL DATE (dates_source = 'hr') IS NEVER TOUCHED. NOTE ON RE-RUNNING: this file RE-MAKES every placeholder each time it is run (so a change of the rules is applied to all of them, and an earlier version's dates are replaced); with the same employees the dates come out exactly the same, but if employees were added in between, the others' placeholders move by a few days (the ranking by seniority moves). When HR gives the real dates, load them with dates_source = 'hr' (a date may also be loaded without any label: it is then simply not a placeholder).
TO UNDO THE PLACEHOLDERS (and only them) at any time: UPDATE public.employee_roster SET date_of_birth = NULL, date_of_joining = NULL, dates_source = NULL WHERE dates_source = 'synthetic';
Like the rest of the roster, nothing here is visible to the AI search's read-only role (it sees only the nlq views, which name their columns).

16_designations.sql : the DESIGNATION LIST put right (step 66c; my request, 1 Nov 2026). Run ONCE in the Supabase SQL editor; safe to run again (a second run changes nothing).
WHAT IT DOES (all in one transaction: if anything fails, nothing is kept)
1. The spelling: "Asst.General Manager" becomes "Asst. General Manager" (a space after the dot), in the list of designations and in the login accounts that carry the old text.

2. ONE "Asst. Manager": the executive designation list had it twice (code 204 with 149 people, code 201 with 95) and a "Junior Manager" (code 201, 1 person), which is not a designation. Nobody is in training today, so these 96 people are Asst. Managers: they move to the code-204 row, KEEP THEIR RELATIVE ORDER, and get new positions after the 149 who are there (rank = grade order x 10000 + position, the HR formula). I then remove the two old rows, but only when nobody holds them.

3. I ADD the training designations, empty (nobody holds them yet): executives Management Trainee (MT) and Junior Officer (JO) code 201, rank 13 (the entry grade, as the old rows were) doctors DNB Doctor code 201, rank 13 <- PLACEHOLDER code non-execs SOT, JOT, TA (in this order, most senior first) codes 400, 399, 398, ranks 25, 26, 27 (below S-1 = 401) <- PLACEHOLDER codes The codes of the doctors' and of the non-executives' training designations are ARBITRARY, chosen to fit the pattern of the others (a higher code is a higher grade). When the right codes are known: UPDATE public.designation_grade SET code = <right code> WHERE title = 'SOT' AND track = 'nonexec'; (and likewise for JOT, TA, 'DNB Doctor') Nothing else needs to change: the employee manager reads the list from this table.
Only public.employee_roster refers to designation_grade (one foreign key), so removing a row nobody holds is safe.

BEFORE YOU RUN IT, to see what it will do (read-only; run this alone): SELECT dg.id, dg.code, dg.title, dg.track, dg.rank_order, count(er.id) AS people FROM public.designation_grade dg LEFT JOIN public.employee_roster er ON er.designation_grade_id = dg.id WHERE dg.code = 201 OR dg.title IN ('Asst. Manager', 'Asst.General Manager') GROUP BY dg.id ORDER BY dg.rank_order, dg.id;
AFTER the new designations exist, run 14_people_events.sql again if you want the sample dates of any trainee to fit (it treats a Management Trainee, SOT, JOT or TA as joined within the last year).

The PDF of an announcement (src/lib/announcements/attachment.ts, src/lib/announcements/admin/files.ts): one row for each announcement that carries a PDF, with or without body text. 29_announcement_search_index.sql

THE SEARCH INDEX OF AN ANNOUNCEMENT (src/lib/announcements/searchIndex/): I prepare it the way a circular is prepared, so that the search bar can find an announcement by its title, by its BODY TEXT and by what its PDF says.

announcement_chunk the passages (about 200 words each) with a vector (768, the same Gemini embedding as circulars): source 'body' = the announcement's own text; source 'pdf' = the PDF, by page. announcement_page the picture of each page of the PDF (kept in Vercel Blob, as circulars keep theirs; the address is never sent to the browser: /api/announcements/<id>/page/<n> serves it). announcement_index one row per announcement: how each part went (ready | failed, and why), how many pages came from the PDF's own text and how many had to be read by AI (OCR), and the PDF's whole text (used for the announcement's own vector and for the answers drawn from it).

I read a true PDF from its own text layer (exact, free); a page with no usable text layer (a scan, an infographic) is read by Gemini, exactly as a circular's pages are. These are tables of their own, so that announcements and their PDFs work whether or not this file has been run (the search then finds titles and body words only). Safe to run more than once. The application also creates the tables by itself the first time something is indexed, if its database user may; running this file is the clean way. Deleting an announcement deletes its rows here (ON DELETE CASCADE); the application deletes the page pictures from Blob.

What I keep about a password's life: when it was last changed (for the 180-day rule), the 5 passwords before it (so they cannot be used again), and the one-time codes of the OTP password change (built, switched off until PASSWORD_OTP=on on the host). The application creates these tables by itself on first use if its database login may (src/lib/security/passwordStore.ts); running this file is the clean way. I keep them closed to the browser: row level security on, nothing granted to anon or authenticated. The history holds bcrypt hashes (as private as the account's own password): do not copy this table anywhere. Safe to run more than once. To start the 180 days again for everybody: DELETE FROM public.password_meta; (each person's clock then begins at his next sign-in; his history is lost)
